stories.title: King to urge AI leaders 'not to lose control of our destiny' at Scotland summit
stories.simple_summary: King Charles is meeting with AI company leaders and asking them to be careful about controlling how AI develops in the future.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly political news — it shows world leaders are paying attention to AI, but it won't directly change what you can do today.

stories.title: The king and AI: U.K. monarch Charles meets with artificial intelligence leaders
stories.simple_summary: King Charles is meeting with people who run AI companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly political news — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: King Charles to call on tech giants for 'reassurances' over AI
stories.simple_summary: King Charles wants AI companies to give assurances that they're being responsible with their technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly political news — it won't affect your daily life or business right now.

stories.title: Iceland-based Treble raises $18 million for its voice simulation platform
stories.simple_summary: A company called Treble raised $18 million to build a tool that copies people's voices using AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and companies making robots or voice products — nothing you need to worry about.

stories.title: Your startup’s next teammate might be an AI agent: Gusto, Insight Partners, and Leland explain what that changes at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
stories.simple_summary: Some startup companies are hiring AI assistants (software that acts like a worker) to work alongside their human employees.
stories.why_it_matters: This is early-stage stuff for tech startups right now, but it hints that small businesses might eventually use AI as team members — mostly relevant to business investors.

stories.title: Snap tries to make the case again for its $2,200 smart glasses
stories.simple_summary: Snap is trying to convince people to buy its expensive smart glasses that cost $2,200.
stories.why_it_matters: Unless you're thinking about buying these glasses, this doesn't affect you — it's a company trying to sell a product.

stories.title: Al Gore says the real AI risk isn’t data centers
stories.simple_summary: Al Gore (a famous environmentalist) says he's not worried about the electricity used by AI, but is more worried about AI safety problems the industry itself has warned about.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a political opinion and not something that directly impacts your everyday life.

stories.title: Snap is launching a new Specs AI tool, and it’s coming to iOS and Mac
stories.simple_summary: Snap is adding a new AI helper to its smart glasses that can connect to your other accounts and help with work tasks like planning travel.
stories.why_it_matters: Unless you use Snap products, this doesn't affect you — it's a new tool for people who already own their glasses.

stories.title: Microsoft AI Chief Says the Way Anthropic Trains Claude Could Upend Society
stories.simple_summary: A Microsoft AI leader says that Anthropic's method of training their AI called Claude could cause big problems for society.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a debate between tech companies about how safe their AI is — it's technical industry news, not something you need to act on.

stories.title: Anthropic and OpenAI want to embed safety evaluators. Will they really be independent?
stories.simple_summary: AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic want to hire independent people to check if their AI is safe, though some worry these checkers might not be truly independent.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about how AI companies oversee themselves — mostly technical industry news, nothing you need to worry about personally.

stories.title: The 2.5-hour AI-generated Odyssey movie is 2.5 hours too long
stories.simple_summary: Someone made a whole movie about The Odyssey entirely using AI, and it turned out to be very bad.
stories.why_it_matters: This is entertainment news showing that AI movies still aren't very good — nothing that affects you unless you wanted to watch it.

stories.title: The AI data center e-waste problem is huge — and getting bigger
stories.simple_summary: AI companies are producing massive amounts of electronic waste (broken computer parts), and by 2050 there could be enough trash to fill millions of shipping containers.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a real environmental problem that could affect your community long-term, similar to how pollution affects everyone, but there's nothing specific you can do about it right now.
